entries.what: ⛔⛔ A FETCH THAT FAILED CAN ANCHOR A CITATION, AND ONE DID — IN A SUBMISSION MANUSCRIPT'S REFERENCE LIST. `lint_citations`' anchor test is 'this identifier appears in a tracked .json', not 'a SUCCESSFUL fetch of it exists'. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-27, and only because an unrelated CI run removed the false anchor. `fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md:63` cites DOI 10.1089/nat.2024.0072 (Andersson et al., Nucleic Acid Ther 35:16-33). It was anchored by THREE records in research/literature/browser-fetch.json, every one of them a 403 whose stored text was a bot-protection interstitial and whose own note read '403 persisted under a real browser; not an IP or header-string problem and not fixable by retrying'. Three records saying WE COULD NOT READ THIS satisfied a gate that exists to establish that somebody did. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION: `git show 372a065cd~1:…browser-fetch.json | grep -c` returns 3 and the same command at 372a065cd returns 0. That commit is a caller-supplied browser fetch that replaced TARGETS via BROWSER_TARGETS_JSON — BY DESIGN, and the file says so in `_targets_overridden`, so the CI job is NOT the defect and must not be filed as one. The gate did not break when the record vanished; it stopped being lied to. ⛔ AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS PAYING FOR, stated in CLAUDE.md §4 in as many words: 'an absent reading is not a reading of absence, and a populated field is not a measured one… presence is never evidence of provenance'. The anchor test is a presence test. ⭐ SCOPE, MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED: seven tracked json/jsonl carry non-2xx fetch records (arxiv-aso-route, preprint-host-eligibility, venue-fee-pages-2026-08-24, venue-policy-browser-fetch, emc-ret-cistrome{,-inputs}, and the now-rewritten browser-fetch), with 35-42 non-2xx status values each in the literature ones. Removing all six from the anchor set leaves exactly FOUR prose identifiers that lose their only anchor: GEO GSE118725, GEO GSE186197, GEO GSE186199, PMID 30413482. ⚠ THAT FOUR IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT THE ANSWER — those files also hold successful records, and being in a file that CONTAINS failures is not the same as being anchored BY one. The real work is the per-record check: an identifier counts as anchored only if it appears inside a record whose own status says the fetch succeeded. ★ THE FIX IS TO MAKE THE ANCHOR PREDICATE READ THE RECORD, not the file. A record carrying a 4xx/5xx status, an explicit failure note, or no retrieved content anchors NOTHING. Then re-run and see which of the four (or fewer) genuinely need a provenance-ledger entry recording who checked them. ⚠ AND DO NOT SOLVE IT BY DELETING THE FAILURE RECORDS: a recorded 403 is real evidence that a route is closed — venue-policy-browser-fetch exists precisely to prove which publisher pages refuse a real browser — it is simply not evidence that a CITATION is real. Two different questions, one file. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-28, CYC-0034-schedule. lint_citations.py’s anchor scan now parses each tracked .json, walks it, and blanks (to `{"url": None, "status": <code>}`) the content of any record shaped like `{"url", "attempts": [...], "status"}` whose own top-level `status` is not a 2xx int — `_is_fetch_record` / `_fetch_succeeded` / `_redact_failed_fetches`, applied before the existing PATTERNS regex runs. Scoped to `.json` only (no tracked `.jsonl` currently uses this shape) and to the exact three-key signature so an unrelated int `attempts` counter (ledger rows) or a bare retry counter is never mistaken for an HTTP fetch log. ⭐ MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, THAT THIS IS SAFE ON THE CURRENT TREE: diffed raw-text vs redacted-text extraction across all seven named corpora (arxiv-aso-route, browser-fetch, preprint-host-eligibility, venue-fee-pages-2026-08-24, venue-policy-browser-fetch, emc-ret-cistrome{,-inputs}) — zero identifiers removed by redaction on any of them, so the specific DOI this defect found (already cleared by the unrelated CI rewrite the ledger row describes) was the only live instance and no new ledger entries were needed. `lint_citations.py` unchanged at 98 unanchored / exit 0. Four new regression tests added to research/modalities/tests/test_lint_citations.py (14 passed, up from 10); `_is_fetch_record` and `_fetch_succeeded` each mutation-tested single-site, caught both times, restored.

⛔ AUT-PROP-022's REWRITE WENT THE RIGHT DIRECTION AND LANDED WRONG IN FOUR OF FIVE PLACES, AND IT BROKE TWO SENTENCES GRAMMATICALLY IN THE PAPER WE WOULD SUBMIT. THE FINDING: a lease-with-TTL solves LIVENESS and cannot solve SAFETY — expiry happens on the lease service's clock, not inside the holder's execution, so a holder suspended past its own expiry still believes it holds the lease and no amount of clock-checking closes the gap. Mutual exclusion must be enforced at the RESOURCE: Chubby's sequencer passes a lock-generation number that the FILE SERVER validates, not the client. Where a write path genuinely cannot check a token, Chubby's fallback is a lock-delay — the lock stays unacquirable for a cooldown after an abnormal release.

⚠ VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: `research/autonomy/claim.py` (built for AUT-PD-021, measured against two real racing workers) ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THE CORE PRIMITIVE and its own docstring names AUT-PROP-030 twice. `git push` IS the fencing check — a compare-and-swap on the remote ref that only succeeds if the remote is still where the claimant thought — so a rejected push is read as 'I LOST THE LEASE', never 'retry harder', with up to 3 retries and a `--check` mode that reports claims held locally the trunk cannot see.

⛔ BUT A SECOND DEFECT WAS MEASURED 2026-08-28 AGAINST A REAL BARE REMOTE AND TWO REAL WORKERS, IN THE SAME SESSION THAT FILED THIS ROW, AND IT IS STILL OPEN: after a rejected push, `reset --soft` + `restore --staged` unstages the claim but LEAVES IT SITTING IN THE WORKING TREE; the subsequent `git merge origin/main` then refuses verbatim ('Your local changes to research/autonomy/research-ledger.json would be overwritten by merge'), `integrate()` returns False, the caller is told to resolve a merge conflict by hand, and the immediate `git merge --abort` fails with 'There is no merge to abort' — there was never a real conflict, only stale work sitting in the tree blocking the refreshed base. THIS IS THE ONE CASE THE MODULE EXISTS FOR (real ledger contention between two workers) failing on contact. The module's own docstring names the fix shape: 'in an optimistic-concurrency loop the re-application IS the loop body, not an optimisation' — the claim's WORK must be recomputed against the refreshed base, not merely have its base pointer moved. SEPARATELY: `push()`/`fetch()` both collapse 'remote unreachable' (a bad pushurl, rc=128) and 'remote refused the compare-and-swap' into one boolean, so a network fault burns all 3 retries and is reported as contention. THE FINDING, THREE PARTS: (1) Kubernetes' own docs name the classic bug of collapsing checks into one board — a dependency check inside LIVENESS (self-only → restart) rather than READINESS (self + dependencies → route away, NEVER restart) means a dependency blip fails liveness on every replica at once, restarting everything into a cold-start herd against the very dependency that just blipped; PROGRESS (work advancing) is a third, separate axis neither covers. (2) Neither OTP nor systemd nor Kubernetes lets a health check retry forever silently — OTP's `intensity`/`period` and systemd's `StartLimitBurst`/`StartLimitIntervalSec` make repeated failure ESCALATE TO A HUMAN after a bounded count, rather than retrying indefinitely. (3) `sd_watchdog_enabled()` returns THREE values (armed / not-armed / error), where `os.environ.get(VAR, default)` collapses all three into 'fine' and fails open silently.

⚠ VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: `research/autonomy/health.py` already exists and already reports ok/red/unmeasured per named condition (`c_cycle_delivering`, `c_advancing_live_work`, `c_evidence_moving`, `c_blocks_are_real`, `c_queue_is_takeable`, `c_cycles_are_sized`, `c_fanout_is_governed`, `c_budget_recovering`, `c_gates_green`, `c_authority_respected`), but it is a FLAT LIST — nothing in it is explicitly tagged liveness vs readiness vs progress, so the k8s failure mode (a readiness-shaped check wired to trigger a restart-shaped response) cannot be ruled out by inspection alone. Verified separately: no restart-intensity counter exists anywhere in research/autonomy/*.py (grepped for 'restart_intensity', 'StartLimitBurst', 'escalat*' — only prose mentions of escalation, no computed burst/period counter), and `research/autonomy/await_ci.py` and `gates_verdict.py` both still read `os.environ.get(VAR, default)` on paths that decide which repo/token to hit — the exact two-valued-collapse pattern this section warns against, though neither is currently flagged as 'safety-relevant' in this repo's own terms.

TASK: (a) tag each existing `health.py` condition liveness/readiness/progress and check that nothing readiness-shaped is wired to a restart-equivalent response (this repo's closest analogue to a restart is a session's automatic hand-off/respawn); (b) add a restart-intensity counter so a condition that goes red on N consecutive dispatches escalates to trimcrae under CLAUDE.md §3 rather than the loop silently retrying forever; (c) audit every `os.environ.get(X, default)` call on a path that gates a real decision (starting with `await_ci.py`/`gates_verdict.py`) and replace the ones that matter with a three-valued read that distinguishes 'set correctly' / 'unset, using default' / 'set but unreadable'.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s34-healthaxes, merged at 975b0b7). (a) AXIS AUDIT: 1 liveness / 5 readiness / 5 progress, tagged in health.py's CONDITION_AXIS. ⭐ THE VERDICT IS NOT 'CLEAN': one readiness-shaped condition IS wired to the restart-equivalent — `authority_respected`, the only `blocks` row — AND THAT IS CORRECT AND DELIBERATE. k8s forbids restarting on a dependency because a restart cannot FIX it; it says nothing about a dependency whose red means CONTINUING DOES IRREVERSIBLE HARM, and an outward act with no grant under trimcrae's name and ORCID is that case. The real defect was that it was UNBOUNDED: refuse → receipt → die → Routine fires → identical refusal, forever. Also measured: handoff.py mentions health.py in 8 prose comments and READS THE BOARD ZERO TIMES, so the respawn restart-equivalent is wired to no condition at all. Both facts are now machine-checked, and a readiness row may only sit on `blocks` if declared in READINESS_MAY_BLOCK with a reason and covered by the counter. (b) RESTART INTENSITY N=5, from systemd's DefaultStartLimitBurst=5 (verified by live search, not recall — freedesktop.org and erlang.org are both EGRESS_BLOCKED). OTP's default intensity=1 was REJECTED as too tight for this loop (one transient red on a half-written ledger would escalate, and this repository has already paid for an over-crying alarm); k8s CrashLoopBackOff is the counter-example, backing off forever and telling nobody. ⛔⛔ MERGING A SEAT'S BRANCH DOES NOT CLOSE THE SEAT'S LEDGER ROW, SO FINISHED WORK IS RE-OFFERED AS READY AND A SECOND SESSION CLAIMS IT. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-28 and it cost a dispatch: `stuck_clock.py` (AUT-PROP-029) was merged to main from a worktree branch — 569 lines, 40 tests, 17/17 mutations — and the row stayed `in_progress` with the SEAT as owner. priority.py's stale-lease sweep then released it, continuity.py offered it as ready, and CYC-0044-schedule claimed it and dispatched a background worktree agent to build what was already on its own base. ⭐ THE SHAPE IS THE LEASE DEFECT ONE STEP LATER: a lease says who HOLDS a row and nothing says who FINISHED one, so the ledger's only record of completion is a human remembering to write it during a merge — which is exactly the 'agreement in prose between a reader and a writer' this repository has now paid for at AUT-PD-013, AUT-PROP-013 and AUT-PD-037. ★ THE FIX IS TO DERIVE IT, NOT TO REMEMBER IT: a merge that lands a seat's deliverable can be detected — the row names its artifact in `depends_on_evidence` or its branch in `lease_released`, and git can answer whether that artifact is on main. A check that refuses to offer a row as READY while its named deliverable already exists on the trunk would have caught this before the dispatch. ⚠ DO NOT auto-close on that signal alone — an artifact existing is not the same as the item being finished, and a row whose deliverable partly landed must stay open. Report it and make a human or the merging session confirm. ⛔⛔ SECOND INSTANCE, SAME DAY: AUT-PROP-032's residue gate (1,110 lines, preflight gate 16) was merged locally and not pushed, the row stayed open on the trunk, and CYC-0046-schedule claimed it and dispatched an agent. ⭐ THE TWO TOGETHER SHARPEN THE FIX: the defect is not that a merge fails to close a row, it is that NOTHING VERIFIES A MERGE HAPPENED. The check now exists — queue_view.already_landed() compares a row's named deliverable against origin/main and caught AUT-020 on its first run — and should be pointed at rows owned by a COMPLETED seat, not only at ready rows.

✅ DONE 2026-08-28 (CYC-0047-cyc0047s, second item this session). Widened already_landed() from ready-rows-only to also cover HELD rows: added queue_view.held_full_rows() (the full ledger row for every live lease, since held()'s own summary dict carries no `what`/`lease_released` for named_paths() to scan), wired it into main() as a new '⛔⛔ HELD, BUT ALREADY ON origin/main' section, and folded it into --check's exit code. Report-only, same as the ready-row half -- never auto-closes, per the module's own stated limit. Regression-tested: research/autonomy/tests/test_the_arbitration_half_of_the_queue_is_visible.py gained 3 cases, the key one (test_a_held_rows_landed_deliverable_is_caught_where_ready_only_missed_it) modelling AUT-PROP-032's exact shape and asserting BOTH that the pre-fix ready-only check sees nothing for an in_progress/owned row AND that the new held-row check does -- all 3 confirmed failing (AttributeError) against the pre-fix module before being trusted, all pass post-fix.

✅ DONE 2026-08-27 (CYC-0025). atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py's main() now compares the committed artifact's own `series` field against the module's SERIES constant BEFORE the derive-reproduces comparison, failing with a named SERIES MISMATCH diagnostic even when fresh == committed -- closing the exact gap the incident exploited (a restore that swaps the inputs cache and the artifact together, both self-consistently wrong, so the derive-reproduces check alone stays green). New regression test test_check_would_have_caught_the_incident_the_drift_check_missed faithfully reproduces the incident's shape (derive() on mutated inputs genuinely equals the mutated committed fixture, not a hand-patched approximation) and is mutation-tested: reverting the fix makes it fail with rc==0, a genuine silent pass. A static assertion of the same invariant already existed (test_the_declared_series_is_the_one_the_committed_artifact_holds) but only ran when the test suite ran; this closes the module's own --check path directly.

⚠ CORRECTION 2026-08-27, appended not edited (CLAUDE.md §1.2), AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE FIX HAD TO BE. This entry says an unrelated restore commit (4a7030e, 2026-08-26) swept in a stale snapshot of the toolchain; CYC-0025's commit message inherits that account. ⛔ IT IS WRONG, and I verified it myself with git rather than taking the reviewing seat's word: `git show --name-only 4a7030e` touches THREE files — research-ledger.json, the ASO archive manifest and step1-fanout-map.json — and NOT the ATR artifact or either cache. The actual clobber was **325258cb8** (2026-08-07), whose own subject line is 'GEO series GSE28866: sample-level characterisation (CI)' and whose entire diff is exactly the three ATR files. It was a direct `mode=gse-series series=GSE28866` dispatch writing the slot it was told to write — not a restore. ⭐ THE DISTINCTION IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: a restore-caused clobber argues for guarding restores, and a dispatch-caused one argues for binding the artifact's IDENTITY, which is what the single-slot registry does and what a 17-line series comparison inside one `main()` does not. The wrong cause would have justified the smaller fix. ⚠ AND HOW LONG THE SLOT WAS WRONG IS NOT PROVEN: this clone is shallow (118 commits), so '2026-08-07 to 2026-08-27' is the interval between the two commits that are readable here, not a demonstrated continuous state.

✅ REVIEWED AND COMPLETED 2026-08-27. A second seat, already holding the problem, was redirected from building to REVIEWING what CYC-0025 landed — and its verdict was that the landed fix is CORRECT BUT NOT COMPLETE: **4 of 8 mutations passed silently on it.** ⛔ THE THREE THAT MATTER. (1) A LIVE HOLE: when the artifact is ABSENT, `--check` writes a fresh artifact and returns 0 BEFORE the series comparison runs, so a deleted artifact plus a wrong-series cache left the slot holding GSE28866 with a green exit. (2) It never looked at the CITING MANUSCRIPTS at all — proven by re-pointing §8 of emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md to the wrong accession on a copy: `--check` rc=0, modalities tests 13/13 pass, and the default preflight log byte-identical to its control. That is the original defect's own shape and it was still undetectable. (3) NOTHING RAN IT before a mistake could be shared: `--check` was in no preflight gate, and the one workflow calling it swallows the exit code by design (`|| echo "non-blocking, but READ IT"`). ⭐ LANDED: the FULL patch, not the minimal one — `research/modalities/single_slot_identity.py`, a REGISTRY that binds the producer constant (read by `ast`), the artifact, each cache, a member-set binding for caches with no identity field, the systems-map entry, and every manuscript declaring a `**Producer:**` block for the slot — plus 17 tests and two rows in preflight gate 11, which is the default commit loop. 8/8 mutations caught against the landed fix's 4/8. The minimal 32-line alternative reached 5/8 and was declined: the manuscript-binding half is precisely what would have caught the original incident. ⚠ IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT police every file mentioning the artifact — 26 lines repo-wide name it alongside another GSE accession and all 26 are legitimate (the ledger, two receipts, a review seat recording this incident verbatim, a precedent citation, a provenance note) — and it does not verify the artifact's PAYLOAD is about the declared series.

✅ DONE 2026-08-27. ⛔ NOTHING ALLOCATES AN ID OF ANY KIND IN THIS LOOP, AND THE SAME COLLISION FIRED TWICE IN ONE HOUR ON TWO DIFFERENT ID SPACES — measured 2026-08-27, not hypothesised. ⭐ THE SECOND INSTANCE IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES IT: this cycle and its sibling ALSO both filed ledger entries numbered AUT-PROP-009 and AUT-PROP-010, from the same max+1 derivation over the same committed ledger, for four entirely different items (RT-PARTNER-STRAT guards here, RT-ATR-ASSESS fixes there). Caught only by a rebase conflict on the ledger; the cycle-id half was caught only because the two claims raced on one push window. So the defect is not about cycle ids, it is about EVERY id the loop mints as max+1 from committed state — cycle ids, AUT-PROP entry ids, and anything later given the same treatment. This cycle derived 'CYC-0016' from the receipts directory; a sibling session that started ~50 s later derived the same id from the same committed state and committed c1bc934 'CYC-0016: claim AUT-010'. Both would have written research/autonomy/receipts/CYC-0016.json, and the ledger's `owner` field would have named one id for two different sessions on two different items. The collision was caught only because a rebase put the two claims side by side; had they not raced on the same push window, the second receipt would have silently overwritten the first. ⭐ THE DERIVATION IS THE BUG: every session computes the id from the same committed state, so concurrency is outside the derivation by construction, and the loop's own architecture assumes cycles are serial when nothing enforces that. Tiebreak taken here was ad-hoc — claimed first (04:20:40Z vs 04:21:20Z), landed second, so this cycle renumbered itself to CYC-0017 — and an ad-hoc tiebreak is not a mechanism. ⚠ FIX THE ALLOCATION, NOT THE TIEBREAK: an id that cannot collide (the session id, or a receipt filename carrying it) beats a rule about who yields, because the yielding session must first NOTICE, and a session that pushes cleanly never does. Check `health.py` too: `cycles_are_sized` reads receipts by session_id and would mis-group two sessions sharing a cycle id. ⛔⛔ THIRD INSTANCE, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE COMMITTED LEDGER: `AUT-PD-012` IS USED TWICE, by two entirely different process defects — CYC-0011's 'the harness reported exit code 0 for a backgrounded preflight that FAILED' and CYC-0015's 'the ledger's retry budget governs nothing'. Those cycles were SEQUENTIAL, not concurrent, which kills the comfortable reading that this is a race: the derivation collides on its own. Present at 053a821 and on origin/main, so it predates CYC-0017 and has been sitting there unnoticed — nothing in the loop validates id uniqueness, so a duplicate is invisible until a human or a rebase trips over it. ⭐ THE FIX THEREFORE HAS TWO PARTS AND THE SECOND IS THE CHEAP ONE: allocate ids so they cannot collide, AND add a uniqueness assertion over `entries[*].id` to priority.py or the gate set, which would have caught all three instances at the commit that created them. De-duplicating the existing AUT-PD-012 pair belongs to this item.

⭐ WHAT SHIPPED: `research/autonomy/ids.py` is the one place that mints an id. `next_receipt()` builds `CYC-<ordinal>-<8 chars of the session id>`, so two sessions reading identical committed state get two different files — the ordinal is deliberately still SHARED, because two concurrent cycles genuinely are both the Nth cycle anybody had committed, and what the record needs is for both to survive saying so rather than for one to be renamed into a lie about its place. The discriminator comes from the SESSION and never from a clock or a counter: a timestamp collides when two sessions start in the same second, and a counter is the derivation that failed. `next_entry_id()` is honestly still max+1 and SAYS SO in its docstring — ledger entries merge through git, so the value there is that the derivation is written down once instead of re-eyeballed by every session, which is how AUT-PD-012 was issued twice by two cycles that never overlapped. `duplicate_ids()` is the cheap half that would have caught all three instances at the commit that created them, and `priority.py` now REFUSES (exit 3) a ledger carrying one rather than ranking it. ⚠ HISTORY IS NOT RENUMBERED: receipts on the trunk keep their bare ids, `receipt_schema.cycle_number()` parses both shapes, and a test asserts it — if a discriminated id parsed as None, every new receipt would silently fall into the grandfathered set and the fan-out gate built this morning would stop governing anything. The committed ledger currently has ZERO duplicates, so the AUT-PD-012 pair the ticket names was already de-duplicated. ✅ 11 tests, 8/8 mutations caught on a scratch copy. ⛔ TWO FINDINGS FROM MY OWN TESTING, BOTH WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE: (1) the module's first draft guarded `next_receipt` with an `os.path.exists` check that was UNREACHABLE — the ordinal is max+1, so the path it returns can never already exist — and only its test's DID NOT RAISE exposed it; the guarantee moved to the WRITE, where a caller really can hand over an existing path, and `x` mode makes the filesystem enforce it. (2) FOUR mutations first appeared to SURVIVE and three of them had never landed — a shell-escaping bug in my own harness. Landing assertions (`s.count(old) == 1` before reading any result) turned three phantom survivors into three catches and left ONE real gap: `write_receipt` with mode `w` passed every test, because the allocator advances the ordinal and the honest flow never asks the write to overwrite. The point of `x` is that it holds when the ALLOCATOR is wrong, which is the whole failure class here, so the test now forces a colliding path.

Three schemas in seventeen receipts, the last drop four cycles after the correct spelling was in use. ⛔ THE CHEAP FIX WAS REFUSED AND THE REFUSAL IS THE POINT: teaching the checker to accept every spelling silently changes the QUANTITY. `launched` is the serial total over a cycle; `subagent_width` caps CONCURRENCY (autonomy-state.json `_subagent_width_means`, and the 107-agent incident was ONE fan-out of width 107). Six sequential agents under a cap of 5 would have read as a violation and five concurrent would have been indistinguishable from five in sequence. ⭐ THE FIX: `research/autonomy/receipt_schema.py` owns the name for BOTH sides — health.py imports `WIDTH_KEY` and `width_of()` rather than spelling them — and a new preflight gate runs `receipt_schema.py --check` at the commit that lands a receipt, which is the only moment anything can check a writer that does not exist (step 10 says 'write the receipt' and every cycle hand-authors the JSON). health.py's diagnostic now NAMES the drifted spelling instead of counting the absence. ⚠ PRE-CUTOFF RECEIPTS ARE GRANDFATHERED BY A CYCLE NUMBER, NOT A LIST: a receipt is immutable committed history, so failing the gate on CYC-0014's spelling would latch it red forever — the defect that wedged the loop the same morning — and the drift is REPORTED rather than hidden, because the ticket was filed against a checker that hid what it could not read. ✅ 21 tests, 10/10 mutations caught on a scratch copy; the mutation that raised the cutoff to 999 passed everything until a test bound it to the newest receipt on the trunk (a suite that exercises one value of a constant measures nothing about the others — the same finding that pinned `in_progress` in the continuity suite). ⚠ STILL OPEN, filed as AUT-PD-017: the general form. Every other cross-file key this loop shares is agreed in prose and checked by nothing.

PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §3 (self-driving-lab SOURCE evidence: A-Lab, Polybot, ARIS; NSLS-II's Adjudicator). THE FINDING: 'out of ideas' is a NAMED, TERMINAL condition in every long-running autonomous-science loop surveyed — A-Lab runs 'until the target is obtained as the majority phase or all synthesis recipes available ... are exhausted'; Polybot terminates 'when the experiment exceeds two weeks or when the measured conductivity do not show further improvement' (a two-clause rule: wall-clock budget OR no further improvement); ARIS's version is a watchdog on empty iterations, empty round → re-plan, FOUR empty rounds → escalate to a human. Separately, NSLS-II's Adjudicator deduplicates incoming suggestions against a bounded `DequeSet(maxlen=100)` of prior proposal ids so one agent cannot flood the queue by re-proposing the same idea.

⛔ THIS REPOSITORY DOES NOT HAVE THIS STATE, AND IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN ONCE AND LEFT UNADOPTED: the FIRST prior-art scan (research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art.md, its ARIS row) already named ARIS's four-empty-rounds watchdog as directly transferable and it was never built. Do not confuse it with what DOES exist: `health.py`'s `c_advancing_live_work` is a LOOP-WIDE, CROSS-CYCLE check — red on 3 consecutive cycle receipts all recording `route_advanced: none` — which catches the loop as a whole doing documentation instead of research (CLAUDE.md §0). AUT-PROP-035's 'out of ideas' is a narrower, PER-ROUTE or PER-LEDGER-ITEM condition: a specific route or research question that has had genuine attempts and stopped improving, distinct from the loop overall being idle. Verified: no per-route stall/no-improvement state, and no admission-dedup mechanism, exists anywhere in research/autonomy/*.py.

TASK: give a route or ledger item its own 'out of ideas' terminal condition — a two-clause rule (a wall-clock budget on the route OR N consecutive attempts producing no measured improvement) with ARIS's four-empty-rounds-escalates-to-a-human as the concrete threshold to adapt — as a companion to (not a replacement for) `stuck_clock.py`'s `stalled_needs_human` (AUT-PROP-029), which detects NO CHANGE AT ALL rather than repeated genuine attempts that keep failing to improve. Separately, add an Adjudicator-style bounded dedup set so a session cannot keep re-filing the same AUT-PROP idea into the ledger queue across cycles.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s35-outofideas, merged at 91fb630): research/autonomy/out_of_ideas.py (two-clause rule — C1 wall-clock READ from priority-weights.json age_saturates_days, never typed; C2 EMPTY_ROUNDS_TO_HUMAN=4 from ARIS, adopted as a COUNT because a count survives a cadence change where a borrowed duration does not, and locally bracketed by rows' own retry_budget:3) and research/autonomy/proposal_dedup.py (identity = (kind, route, normalized `what`), NOT id — the failure mode is the same idea under a new id; route is in the key because the ledger already carries byte-identical `what` on different routes as correct distinct work, and a text-only key would suppress 39 of 40 legitimate rows). Threshold 0.30 CALIBRATED, not remembered: 1,108 in-bucket pairs of genuinely distinct rows top out at 0.111, a reworded self scores 0.484-0.606, and calibration_probe() re-measures both populations every test run so the day they meet the suite says so. Five verdicts, unmeasurable counts as needing attention (fails closed). 23/23 mutations caught. Live reading: 0 out_of_ideas, 0 unmeasurable, 1 has_ideas, 73 not_attempted, 9 no_open_rows. ⭐ ITS OWN TEST FOUND A REAL BUG: is_attempt_event counted a lease RELEASE (owner→None + attempts+1, written by priority.py:release_stale_claims in one commit) as a second attempt, silently halving every threshold. ⛔ IT IS A REPORTER, NOT ADMISSION CONTROL, UNTIL SOMETHING CALLS IT — see the two follow-up rows.

entries.what:
PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §4.4 (PUBMED 10.1038/s41467-024-55655-3 Polybot, 10.1038/s41467-023-37139-y AlphaFlow). THE FINDING: a result must pass an EXPLICIT VALIDITY PREDICATE, written down IN ADVANCE, before it is allowed to steer the next decision. Polybot runs every sample 2–4 times, applies Shapiro–Wilk at α=0.03 and a two-sample test at α=0.005, discards thickness readings with goodness-of-fit < 0.9, and IQR-filters at scale 1.5 before averaging. AlphaFlow enumerates the signature of a DEAD RUN in advance — undetectable droplet volume, no measurable spectral features, insufficient nanoparticle concentration — and terminates in-line rather than letting a dead run's numbers reach the evidence base. This is the document's own named counter to this repository's worst measured failure: 'env-echoed defaults carrying a fabricated verdict all the way out.'

⚠ THE PATTERN IS ALREADY KNOWN IN THIS REPO FOR ONE DOMAIN, JUST NOT FOR THE LOOP'S OWN EVIDENCE: `scripts/emc_km_admissibility.py` already implements exactly this shape for Kaplan–Meier curve digitization (an explicit, computed 'quality floor' a digitized curve must clear before AUT-034 admits or refuses it) — proving the mechanism is understood here, not that it is generalised. This proposal's target is DIFFERENT and unbuilt: the AUTONOMY LOOP'S OWN EVIDENCE INPUTS — a subagent seat's factual report, a cycle receipt's claims, a ledger row's `score_inputs` block, a claimed environment reading — currently have no computed admission gate at all. Instead this repository relies on a session REMEMBERING to apply CLAUDE.md §4's evidence-discipline rules by hand each time ('an absent reading is not a reading of absence', 'never act on the snapshot that triggered you', 'presence is never evidence of provenance'), which is exactly the 'a thing we remember' this proposal's own score-basis names, and it has already failed once (AUT-PD-026: a subagent's stale environment reading was almost written into the ledger as a live blocker before a second seat measured the real mechanism).

TASK: for one or more of the loop's own evidence types — start with a seat's factual claim in a cycle receipt, or a `score_inputs` block on a ledger row — write down IN ADVANCE the observable signature that makes it INADMISSIBLE (e.g. a factual claim with no cited command/log/diff behind it; a `score_inputs` block copied from a parent without re-deriving; an environment reading older than N minutes relative to when it is filed), and check that signature BEFORE the evidence is allowed to change a ledger row's score, state or `what` field — turning today's prose discipline into a computed gate, the same conversion `emc_km_admissibility.py` already made for one modality.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s36-admissibility, merged at a660303): research/autonomy/admissibility.py, enforced in ledger_io.write_ledger — the one chokepoint AUT-PD-037 already forces every ledger writer through. Evidence type chosen: a row's `score_inputs` block and the `score` it is the audit trail for; the ledger's own `_scores_are_not_evidence` field PROMISED a reader could check the arithmetic and nothing ever did. Signature: unreadable / underivable from pinned weights / accumulated beyond what its own echoed terms account for / stale echoed age_factor; unscored and unaccounted are graded UNMEASURED, never admitted. So each generation is instructed to extend a chain that has a hard ceiling, and the LAST generation is the one told most emphatically to do the impossible — the deeper the loop has run unattended, the more certainly the instruction fails. ⛔ AND THE FAILURE IS RECORDED AS A DEFECT IN THE SESSION RATHER THAN IN THE PLATFORM: `health.py`'s `cycles_are_sized` grades an over-cap session with no `handoff.child_session_id` as RED, and no future cycle can clear that row by behaving better — the same LATCHING shape `RECEIPT_WINDOW` was introduced to fix, arriving through a different door. ⚠ NOT AN OUTAGE: the 'EMC research loop — driver' Routine (13 */4 * * *) is enabled and healthy, so the chain terminating costs a ~4 h delay rather than continuity. That is the backstop working as designed — and it is only NOT a deferral because the handoff was attempted first and refused. ⭐ FIXES WORTH CONSIDERING, none obviously right: (1) handoff.py should CHECK the depth before building a prompt it cannot use, and say plainly that the Routine is the successor when it cannot spawn; (2) `cycles_are_sized` should read a refused-handoff record and grade it as UNMEASURED rather than RED, since 'the platform refused' is not the same fact as 'this session did not hand off'; (3) the child could be spawned by the Routine rather than by the parent, which removes the chain entirely. ⛔ Do NOT fix this by raising the cap on cycles per session — the cap is about context running out silently and has nothing to do with the spawn limit.

⛔ CANDIDATE (1) CANNOT BE BUILT, and whoever reads this next should not try: `handoff.py` cannot check the lineage depth before building its prompt. It is a pure-stdlib script with no network and no session context; the depth is known only to `create_session` at call time. The refusal is discoverable ONLY by attempting the handoff. ⭐ SO THE FIX IS CANDIDATE (2), AND IT IS THE ONE THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT ALREADY ARGUED FOR: `c_cycles_are_sized` says in its source that 'a condition that cannot be satisfied by doing the right thing ... is a stopwatch, not a guard'. Green would claim the rule was satisfied; red claims a defect that is not the session's; unmeasured says the loop cannot be graded on this because the mechanism was gone. ⛔ AND THE REFUSAL MUST BE RECORDED VERBATIM — an absent or whitespace record stays RED, or 'I could not' becomes a free pass claimable by any session that never tried. ✅ 5 new tests; 4 mutations, 4 caught, control green at 74, both files restored byte-identically by sha256 comparison. ⚠ AND TWO MUTATION HARNESSES WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST: one returned `8 failed, 66 errors` uniformly and one had a control of `3 failed`, because the file copies were not faithful. Both would have printed a tidy table of catches. A mutation run whose CONTROL IS NOT GREEN measures nothing, and the tidy table is what makes that dangerous. ⭐ CANDIDATE (3) — the Routine spawning the child instead of the parent — remains open and is the only one that removes the chain rather than accommodating it. Filed as the real fix; this is the honest accounting of a ceiling, not a way past it.

TASK: express this repository's claim ceilings IN GRADE TERMS, not necessarily by adopting GRADErater itself — e.g. map each R1–R5 category, or each claim scoped to a `TECH-*` readiness tag, to the GRADE certainty rating its evidence actually supports, so a reviewer or outside reader can tell how strong a claim is allowed to be WITHOUT first learning this repository's own R1–R5 glossary. entries.what:
PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §4.3 (PUBMED 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2017.08.008, Simmonds et al. 2017, Living systematic reviews: 3). THE FINDING: repeated looks at accumulating evidence inflate type I error — 'the chance of incorrectly concluding that any updated meta-analysis is statistically significant when there is no effect increases rapidly as more updates are performed.' Four published fixes exist: the law of the iterated logarithm and the Shuster method (type I error only), and trial sequential analysis / sequential meta-analysis (type I AND II, with heterogeneity). SIMMONDS' OWN DECISION RULE IS THE PART TO STEAL: if the review only reports the CURRENT BEST PICTURE and readers know results may change, standard methods are fine; if the updated conclusion FEEDS A DECISION, the sequential correction is required.

WHY THIS BEARS ON THE AUTONOMY LOOP SPECIFICALLY (not just the manuscripts): this repository's research loop repeatedly RE-EXAMINES THE SAME CLAIMS as new evidence accumulates across cycles — a route's score is re-derived from `systems/graph` on every ledger `--write`, a blocker's status is re-checked cycle over cycle, and `research/method-watch.md` explicitly re-grades settled findings on a schedule as methods improve (CLAUDE.md §4: 'that licenses keeping the option open and re-grading it on a schedule; it never licenses claiming a result early'). That is structurally identical to a living systematic review's repeated-look problem, and §4.3's own framing is direct: 'nobody in the LLM wave has this.' Verified: no sequential-testing or repeated-look correction exists anywhere in this codebase (grepped for 'sequential test', 'type I error', 'iterated logarithm', 'Shuster' — no hits outside the survey document itself).

Instrumented, not argued: `git show HEAD:research/autonomy/research-ledger.json` and the tree after a fresh `priority.py --write` BOTH report 271 entries / 103 with `score is None` / 94 with no `score` key, and the SET of unscored ids is IDENTICAL before and after — re-scoring moves none of them.

And `health.py:queue_is_takeable` cannot see any of this: it reports TAKEABLE off the scored rows, so the ledger could reach 100% unscored real work and the stall condition would still print green on one derived row. An absent score is being read as a reading of absence (CLAUDE.md §4).
⚠ THE COST IS POINTED STRAIGHT AT CLAUDE.md §0. Of the 79 open unowned unscored rows, 26 are NOT RT-AUTONOMY and several are live in-silico work: AUT-PROP-048 (RT-SGK1, '$0 AND THE INPUTS ARE ON DISK: score NDRG1 against HIF-1 and PPARγ target panels in the two committed expression series'), AUT-PD-110 (RT-ALK-HIT re-grade against PMID 42660639), AUT-PD-005 (RT-DEGRADER-TERNARY), AUT-079 / AUT-PD-100 / AUT-PD-102 (RT-JUNCTION-NEOANTIGEN HLA panel). THE LOOP HAS BEEN DOCUMENTING ITSELF BECAUSE THE RESEARCH WAS STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE, not because any cycle chose it.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES ARE NOW DEAD ENDS WITH EVIDENCE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX I DID NOT GET. ⛔ (1) A GIT MERGE DRIVER MAKES IT WORSE, MEASURED NOT REASONED. TWO MORE SHAPES FAIL IDENTICALLY, each found only by fixing the one before it: (a) an ADDITIVE edit's anchor survives its own application — RT-TCIP.artifacts proposes '"ART-TCIP-REACH"' -> '"ART-TCIP-REACH", "ART-TCIP-EFFECTOR-ARMS"', so the old string is a SUBSTRING of the new one and the row could never reach APPLIED by any action; (b) the proposal for that same row spans TWO LINES, and the search is line-at-a-time, so the applied check could only ever answer no.
FIXED: the PENDING question is asked only of each line's LIVE part (up to any supersession marker); an uninformative additive anchor is overridden only by a POSITIVE applied reading; multi-line needles are matched across lines with whitespace collapsed.

This is the arbitration the item asked for: between a lease that LOOKS alive because nobody has re-scored yet, and a ready row sitting behind it. 11 new tests in test_continuity_has_no_green_state_recording_can_buy.py (54 total, all green): self-exclusion of the caller's own lease, within/past the lease window, an unstamped claim treated as stale immediately (mirrors release_stale_claims' fail-toward-releasing direction), would_be_ready_if_released against a second real block vs. the lease being the only block, finished rows excluded, sort order (unstamped first), and the CLI's own output. Mutation-tested by hand against the live tree (no subagent, no concurrent mutation window): reverting the self-exclusion check and reverting the unstamped-is-stale branch each made the corresponding new test fail, then both were restored and the full suite reconfirmed green (54 passed). Verified read against the real ledger: `continuity.py --leases` on the committed ledger correctly reported zero other-held leases once this cycle's own claim was excluded via --me.

Decide whether an entry with no score inputs is unrankable (and say so in the output) or whether the missing inputs have honest defaults, then make the ledger's own schema enforce it. ⛔ AND WIRE IT TO SOMETHING: an unrun ranker is AUT-PD-018 again. ⭐ FIXED: `entry.setdefault("score_inputs", {})` at the penalty line and `(parent.get("score_inputs") or {})` at its sibling — the inheritance line, which would have been the next crash and is the shape `paper-hardening` §8b.2 measured six of eleven list-scoped fixes missing. ⛔ THE JUDGEMENT WENT THE HONEST WAY: the dict is created EMPTY, carrying only the flag this function actually observed, rather than filled with zeroed defaults. entries.what: ⚠ `lint_readability.sentences()` DOES NOT BREAK BEFORE A CALLOUT GLYPH, SO IT REPORTS TWO SENTENCES AS ONE AND OVERSTATES THE LENGTH. The split regex is `(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z(“\"])`, so a sentence opening with ⛔, ⭐, ⚠, ★ or ✅ — the house callout style, used on nearly every emphatic sentence in these manuscripts — is glued to the sentence before it. Two other openers fail the same way and both were hit in this document: a section reference (`§4.3's conservative-floor reading …`) and a sentence following a quotation whose period sits INSIDE the closing quote (`… EMCs.” So the honest reading …`). ⭐ THE DIRECTION MATTERS AND IT IS THE SAFE ONE: the defect makes the screen STRICTER, never laxer, so nothing has been let through by it and no published claim rests on it. That is why it is filed rather than fixed. ⛔⛔ AND IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED FOR A SECOND, BINDING REASON: `lint_readability` IS the instrument behind publish_bar clause 7, clause 7 had just BLOCKED PUB-FUSION-PARTNER, and research-loop §6's invariant is that a bar may not be changed by the cycle the bar just blocked. Fixing the splitter would have retired 2 of the 17 findings without touching the prose — the textbook self-serving edit `amendment_guard` exists to catch. CYC-0070-ba841eee therefore split all 17 in the prose instead, including the 2 whose real sentences were already inside the ceiling. ★ A LATER CYCLE MAY MAKE THE IDENTICAL CHANGE, and should: extend the lookahead to the callout glyphs and to `§`, and treat a closing quote or bracket after terminal punctuation as still terminal. ⛔ MUTATION-TEST IT — a splitter change moves every count in `readability-baseline.json`, so re-pin the baseline in the same commit and state that the counts moved because the instrument did, not because the prose did.

entries.what: ⛔ LEDGER-ENTRY FIELD NAMES ARE HAND-TYPED, WITH NO SCHEMA CATCHING A NEAR-MISS SPELLING — the residual risk AUT-PD-017's sweep found and did not fix (scope: a whole-ledger validator, not a two-file constant-sharing pattern like receipt_schema.py's). Every entry in research-ledger.json is authored directly as JSON by a cycle, and several readers (continuity.py, priority.py, health.py) key off specific field names -- `owner`, `requires_trimcrae`, `blocked_by`, `blocked_evidence`, `closes_clause`, `cost_class`, `retry_budget` -- with no whitelist anywhere that would catch `require_trimcrae`, `requires_trimcrae_` or `owned_by` as a typo rather than a new field. ⛔ THE SHARPEST EDGE IS `requires_trimcrae`: continuity.py's `_why_not_ready()` treats an ABSENT key as 'not outward-facing' (falls through to ready), and `unclassified_outward()` only catches it if the item's own `what` text ALSO matches a regex over publish/submit/deposit/outreach verbs -- so a ledger entry that means to block an outward-facing act via a misspelled key, on text the regex does not match, is silently offered as ready with NO warning at all. That is category (c) from AUT-PD-017's own test (silently reads as GREEN), on the one field CLAUDE.md §3 exists to protect. ⛔ `owner` and `closes_clause` are lower-risk by comparison (a misspelled `owner` just fails to claim the lease, which is the safe direction; a misspelled `closes_clause.clause` reports a paper's blocking clause as still-uncovered, also the safe direction) but belong in the same sweep since the fix is one validator, not three. ⭐ THE FIX SHAPE: a `ledger_schema.py` (or an addition to an existing checker) that owns a whitelist of known top-level ledger-entry field names (including the `_why`-suffixed explanation fields already in use), flags any key within edit distance ~1-2 of a known name that is not itself a known name, and is wired into preflight as a gate over the whole ledger -- no grandfather cutoff needed here since it is a live-edited single file, not immutable receipt history; a one-time hand fix of any existing near-miss is enough before turning the gate on. ⚠ CHEAP AND FREE, same as AUT-PD-013/AUT-PD-017 — no compute, no network.

AUT-PD-138's ordering says regenerate the manifest against a clean tree as the session's LAST commit, so `git_revision` names the content commit it describes. That is what happened: the manifest named 6a4c833fd, `git_tree_is_clean_apart_from_this_manifest: true`, --check-archive exit 0, and both manifest guard modules 11/11. ⛔ THEN TWELVE COMMITS LANDED FROM A CONCURRENT SESSION AND THE REBASE REWROTE 6a4c833fd TO 656ff2a29992. The manifest was now naming a sha that exists ONLY in this container's reflog — unreachable for anybody who clones — while its clean flag still read true and its inventory was still current. ⭐ THE THREE THINGS THAT WOULD CATCH IT ALL LOOK RIGHT: the cleanliness flag is about the TREE, not the ref; --check-archive explicitly does not compare repository-state fields; and `test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve` passes locally because the orphaned sha still resolves through the local reflog. It was caught by hand, by comparing git_revision against `git rev-parse HEAD~1` after the rebase, and nothing required that. ⚠ AND THIS IS THE NORMAL CASE, NOT AN EDGE ONE. A concurrent loop session pushed 12 commits during the ~20 minutes this cycle spent rebuilding a deposit family, and the trunk moved under it three separate times. Any manifest commit that has to be rebased has this defect. WHAT TO DO: the candidate is to make the revision check ask git whether the named sha is an ANCESTOR OF THE COMMITTED BRANCH rather than merely resolvable — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <git_revision> HEAD` — which is false for an orphan and true for a real parent, and which the reflog cannot fake. ⚠ Note it must run against the committed history, not the working tree, or it reintroduces AUT-PD-138's ordering trap. ⛔ DO NOT 'fix' this by regenerating the manifest after every rebase as a convention: that is the remembered pairing AUT-PD-130 is about, and it failed there for the same reason it would fail here.

BixBench3 (arXiv:2608.25286v1) graded 13 frontier models on 20 research-study-scale computational-biology tasks. Excluding those three tasks from EVERY model's average puts Opus 5 second at 0.455, behind 0.458. The failure was instruction-following on a schema, not science.
WHAT TO DO: (1) list every artifact an agent writes in this repository — cycle receipts, review-seat records, health.json, handoff files, generated views, regenerated data artifacts, preflight receipts; (2) for each, say whether a gate would FAIL if the file were emitted with a renamed key, a missing required field, or the right values under the wrong schema; (3) file the unguarded ones. ⛔ DO NOT WRITE GUARDS IN THIS ITEM — the enumeration is the deliverable, because guessing which files matter is how a guard lands on the ones that were already covered. ⚠ MUTATION-TEST anything that follows (paper-hardening: a guard that cannot be made to go red is not a guard). Reading: research/method-watch-bixbench3-calibration.md §5.1
entries._score_basis: free, and it targets the one weakness in this program's own model that an external benchmark has actually measured rather than one we inferred

⭐ GIVE THE LOOP AN EXTERNALLY-ANCHORED FAILURE VOCABULARY — adopt BixBench3's closed ten-tag failure-mode set as an optional `failure_modes` block on the cycle receipt, and measure it in health.py.
WHY IT IS NOT BUSYWORK: method-watch-autonomy-prior-art.md §2 item 3 states the gap plainly — 'this loop has no external calibration of any kind: health.py grades the loop against rules we wrote.' BixBench3 measured that a run's total failure-tag count predicts its score at Spearman rho = -0.92 (p = 9.9e-6), with premature termination (~2.0x) and repetitive retry loop (~2.2x) the most enriched in the worst quantile. Mapping that vocabulary onto CLAUDE.md's own dated incidents lands SEVEN of the ten (repetitive retry loop = the pgrep self-match loops, 2026-08-26; premature termination = the bare `&` orphaned jobs, 2026-08-27; synthetic/placeholder output = the env-echoed fabricated verdict; output format violation = the generated-artifact regime; environment setup failure = the fresh-sandbox import reds, 2026-08-23; incomplete data = 'an absent reading is not a reading of absence'; inefficient analysis = the serialized-preflight complaint, 2026-08-25).
⛔ THE THREE MISSES ARE THE POINT, AND THE ITEM IS NOT DONE WITHOUT THEM: input misinterpretation, wrong method substitution and method misconfiguration have NO dated incident here. They are the SCIENTIFIC execution errors, and the benign reading (we do not make them) is not the only one — an operational failure is loud and a misconfigured method is silent, and nothing in this loop is instrumented to catch the second. State which of the three this loop could actually detect, and say UNMEASURED for the rest rather than shipping a green row. ⚠ A receipt that records no `failure_modes` block must leave the health row UNMEASURED, never green — the exact defect AUT-PD-013 records for `fanout_is_governed`. Reading: research/method-watch-bixbench3-calibration.md §4

entries.what:
✅ FIXED 2026-08-27 by claim.py's own author, the same hour it was filed. claim.py's Git.push() (research/autonomy/claim.py:79-80) runs `git push -q origin main`, which pushes whatever LOCAL BRANCH IS LITERALLY NAMED 'main' -- stale or unrelated to HEAD if the session's real work is on a differently-named branch (e.g. this repo's 'claude/dreamy-hawking-18pm7n' convention, which stays rebased onto origin/main and is pushed via `git push origin <branch>:main`). On such a session, claim.py's push always fails as a non-fast-forward (or pushes nothing new), so the module cannot actually arbitrate a claim there -- it silently degrades to reporting RETRY forever rather than CLAIMED. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (CYC-0028-moriokat, a subagent dispatched by CYC-0027's driver session): claim.py was tried first for AUT-PD-020, failed exactly this way, and the seat fell back to the manual fetch/verify/edit/commit/`push origin HEAD:main` sequence documented as claim.py's own manual fallback -- work completed correctly, but the module meant to make this race-safe took no part in it. FIX (not applied here, filed for a future cycle): push() should push HEAD, not the ref literally named 'main' -- `git push -q origin HEAD:main`, which is a fast-forward-safe compare-and-swap on the REMOTE ref regardless of what the local branch is named, exactly matching the module's own stated design intent.

⭐ APPLIED EXACTLY AS FILED: `Git.PUSH_REFSPEC = ("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main")`. The filing session's diagnosis and its proposed fix were both correct and are taken unchanged. ⛔⛔ THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS HOW IT SURVIVED ITS OWN TEST SUITE: nine tests, eight mutations, and a first real use that reported CLAIMED and pushed — all of it in the ONE configuration that hides the bug, because the author's local branch happened to be named `main`. Every test drove a `FakeGit` that never reaches a real refspec, so the argv was the single thing the suite could not see and the exact thing that was wrong. ⭐ The new test asserts on the argv itself rather than through the fake, which is the only level at which this class of defect is visible. ⚠ AND THE COST WHILE IT WAS OPEN IS THE SHAPE THE MODULE EXISTS TO PREVENT: on a `claude/<name>` branch it did not error loudly, it reported RETRY forever — so a seat trying to claim AUT-PD-020 fell back to the manual fetch/verify/edit/commit sequence and completed the work correctly, while the tool built to make that race-safe took no part in it. A tool that fails by degrading into the manual path it replaced is one nobody notices is broken.

⛔ A REVIEW-SEAT SUBAGENT EDITED THE LIVE TRACKED TREE DURING A READ-ONLY HARDENING ROUND, AND ONLY THE 'STAGE BY PATH, NEVER -A' RULE CAUGHT IT (CLAUDE.md §6). Round 12 of PUB-ASO hardening (AUT-PROP-040) dispatched five parallel blind-review subagents, each explicitly told 'do NOT edit any tracked file in the working tree — this is a read-only review seat' and, if it wanted to mutation-test a guard, to 'make a scratch copy first ... and mutate the COPY, never the live tree.' Mid-round, `git status` showed an UNSTAGED, UNEXPECTED edit to research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md: 'with *TAF15* a substantial minority ⭐ and your *TCF12* and *TFG*' — a nonsensical two-token insertion the driver did not make. Caught only because the driver staged research/manuscripts/submission-metrics.json BY PATH rather than `git add -A`; had -A been used, this would have committed and pushed to `main` inside an otherwise-legitimate commit, matching the shape of the 13-inverted-claims incident this rule already exists to prevent. Reverted immediately with `git checkout --`; no commit ever contained it.

ROOT-CAUSED, NOT GUESSED (CLAUDE.md §4): seat 1 (the regression lens) later reported it had verified this exact mutation 'on a scratch clone (/tmp/.../seat1-clone-real, checked out at the pinned commit, git checkout -- ... used to revert each time)'. The obvious hypothesis — a `cp -al` hardlink clone whose in-place edits leak back to the source inode, the failure mode paper-hardening §8b.1 already documents — was checked directly and REFUTED: `stat -c %i` on the live file (inode 483841) and on the same path inside scratchpad/seat1-clone-real (inode 1886303) are DIFFERENT inodes; seat1-clone-real also carries its own .git directory, confirming it is a real separate checkout, not a hardlinked copy. So the clone itself was not the leak. The mutation must have reached the live path some other way — most plausibly the seat's editing tool was pointed at the live repo path for at least one test before (or instead of) the clone for that specific mutation, and its own revert step ran after the driver's `git status` check happened to land in the open window. The seat's own report and the driver's direct observation cannot both be fully accurate; this entry records the observation (the live-tree diff, with inode evidence) rather than the seat's self-report, per CLAUDE.md §4's own priority of a real diagnostic over an agent's account of its own actions.

⚠ NOT A CATASTROPHE THIS TIME, BUT THE MARGIN WAS ONE HABIT: if the driver had used `git add -A` (a natural shortcut when only one file was actually intended to change), this lands on `main`. The instruction given to seats ('use a scratch copy, never the live tree') is a PLAIN SUGGESTION, not a structural boundary — nothing prevents a general-purpose subagent's editing tool from targeting any path it likes, including the shared live tree, when its cwd is the same repo the driver is sitting in.

PROPOSED FIX (not applied here — scoping only): any future review-seat prompt that even mentions the possibility of mutation-testing should either (a) launch the seat inside an isolated worktree (EnterWorktree / a dedicated git worktree per seat, per research-loop §3's existing worktree guidance for MUTATING subagents) rather than relying on a self-reported scratch copy, or (b) if a true read-only seat only occasionally wants to check mutation robustness, make the instruction a hard constraint naming the exact clone path and explicitly forbidding any tool call from touching a path under the live repo, not a soft 'if you want to test something, use a copy' suggestion. Either way: CLAUDE.md §6's 'stage by path, never -A, while a subagent that mutates the working tree is running' is the backstop that actually worked here and must stay in force even for seats explicitly told they are read-only, since this incident shows that instruction alone is not reliable.

⛔⛔ UPDATE, SAME CYCLE, MORE SEVERE THAN THE NEAR-MISS ABOVE: it did NOT stay a near-miss. While fixing the 'stale submission-metrics.json' preflight failure, the driver ran `python3 research/manuscripts/submission_metrics.py` (the real regeneration, not `--check`) directly against the LIVE WORKING TREE while seat 1 was still active in the same window — and the live article file was contaminated at that exact moment. The regeneration silently captured the contaminated word count (main_words 3721, i.e. the clean 3719 plus the two inserted tokens '⭐'+'your', which this counter's regex apparently both count) and the driver COMMITTED it (6e7d44e06), reading the discrepancy as genuine pre-existing drift rather than live contamination. This is a corrupted-artifact commit that landed on `main`, not merely a caught-in-time diff. It was caught two commits later by round 12's own seat 4 (citations/build/gates lens), which independently regenerated the metric inside an isolated worktree of the PINNED commit and got 3719, flagged the direction of the 'fix' as backwards, and named the exact mechanism. Corrected in 3a53478a8.

★★ THE GENERALISABLE LESSON THIS ADDS, BEYOND THE git add -A RULE ALREADY STATED ABOVE: 'stage by path, never -A' protects the COMMIT boundary, but it does NOT protect a DERIVATION step that reads the live working tree WHILE a mutation-risk subagent is running. `submission_metrics.py` (like `aso_archive_manifest.py` and any other generator that reads files off disk rather than off `git show`) has no way to know the tree it just read was transiently contaminated -- it can only report what the bytes said at read time. The fix that actually worked here was VERIFICATION AFTER THE FACT (a second seat re-deriving the same number against an isolated pinned-commit worktree), not prevention -- which argues for either (a) not running any live-tree-reading regeneration script while review/mutation-risk subagents are still active, deferring such fixes until they have all reported, or (b) always regenerating from a `git stash`-clean or freshly-cloned tree rather than the shared working directory when subagents are concurrently active in it.

⛔ GENERIC FIXED PATHS OUTSIDE THE SCRATCHPAD ROOT ARE AUT-PD-055 ONE LEVEL OUT, and seat_scratch.py --audit-root cannot see them by construction. Measured 2026-08-28 by seat s55-scratchpad while fixing AUT-PD-055: research/autonomy/gates_verdict.py:112 defaults --out to /tmp/gates.json; scripts/venue_typeset_geometry.py:176 defaults --workdir to /tmp/venue-typeset; scripts/triage-literature.mjs:8-9 documents /tmp/idx.json in its usage line, which TEACHES the pattern. Two concurrent callers of any of these overwrite each other with no marker and the second reads the first's file as its own — the same fabricated-but-clean-looking result AUT-PD-055 measured, with nothing watching. ★ FIX: default each to a session/seat-scoped path (or mkdtemp), and keep the usage line teaching the scoped form. Not absorbed into AUT-PD-055 because each is a behaviour change to a shipped script.

⛔ A SEAT-PROMPT CONVENTION THAT LIVES ONLY IN A SKILL BINDS ONLY WHEN THE SKILL IS LOADED — the same reachability gap CLAUDE.md §6 already records for research-loop §3's session shapes, where `"name":"Skill"` appeared 0 times in the transcript of the session that broke the rule. AUT-PD-055's fix is a convention stated in research-loop §3; a driver who dispatches seats without loading that skill gives prompts that omit it, and nothing measures the omission. ★ PROPOSAL: have the cycle receipt record that dispatched seats were given the seat-discipline lines (worktree, seat-scoped logs outside it, EXIT= markers, no ledger edits), and have health.py read that field — the same shape as `fanout_is_governed`, pointed at seat-prompt CONTENT rather than width. ⚠ Design it so an absent field reads UNMEASURED, never green.

PROPOSAL from seat s55-scratchpad (AUT-PD-055), NOT BUILT because it needs a driver-level decision: add a health.py axis that reads the LIVE scratchpad root via seat_scratch.audit_root during a fan-out, so an unowned root file is red WHILE seats are running rather than discovered afterwards. ⛔ THE DECISION IT NEEDS: every existing health.py condition is computed from COMMITTED state, and this one would read per-session state no commit contains — which is a real departure (a checker that reads mutable local state can report a red no other reader can reproduce). Decide that explicitly before building it. Related: seat_scratch.py was deliberately NOT wired into preflight.sh for the same reason — preflight is offline, deterministic and repo-scoped.

⛔⛔ `claim.py` TURNS A ONE-ROW LEASE INTO AN UNGATED PUSH WHEN THE TREE IS DIRTY, AND NOTHING REFUSES IT. Measured 2026-08-28 by CYC-0053-3217966b, on itself: the driver held (a) an unpushed merge commit of seat s55's branch and (b) uncommitted edits to research-ledger.json (a closure plus three new rows), with `./scripts/preflight.sh` STILL RUNNING on that tree. It then ran `claim.py --id AUT-PROP-036`. `Git.commit_ledger` stages research-ledger.json WHOLE, so the uncommitted edits were swept into the claim commit; `PUSH_REFSPEC = ('push','-q','origin','HEAD:main')` then pushed EVERY local commit on HEAD, so the seat merge went to the trunk too. Net: 467 lines of new code and 64 lines of ledger reached origin/main with the gate that was supposed to clear them still in flight. ⚠ THE GATE DID NOT FAIL — IT WAS BYPASSED, which is the same shape as AUT-PD-0xx's `git add -A` mutation window: a narrow tool that stages by FILE and pushes by BRANCH cannot distinguish the one row it was asked to lease from whatever else the working tree happens to be holding. It is silent by construction, and the driver only noticed by reading `git show --stat` afterwards. (This run came back green — EXIT=0, log s0-preflight-s55merge-2.log — so nothing was broken. A green outcome is not the finding; the absent refusal is.) ★ FIX, and the choice matters: `claim.py` should REFUSE to run when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty outside the ledger row it is about to write, or when HEAD is ahead of origin/main by commits it did not author — printing what it found, so the caller commits and gates deliberately. ⛔ DO NOT 'fix' this by having claim.py stage a partial hunk or push a detached ref: the claim's whole safety argument is that the push is an atomic compare-and-swap on the trunk (AUT-PROP-030), and anything that makes the push narrower than HEAD weakens the arbiter. The honest fix is a refusal, not a cleverer push. ⚠ AND WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the refusal must not deadlock the ordinary loop, where a cycle legitimately holds a ledger edit and a claim at once — decide explicitly whether 'dirty' means the ledger file itself (usually legitimate) or anything else (never legitimate), and mutation-test both directions.

⛔ `proposal_dedup.Adjudicator.admit()` IS BUILT, CALIBRATED AND CALLED BY NOTHING — the exact 'a rule that governed nothing' shape CLAUDE.md §1 records twice (subagent_width governed nothing for days; the fan-out receipt key was agreed in prose and lost twice). Nothing in the cycle contract currently files a new AUT-PROP row through a chokepoint, so the module decides and reports while every re-filed idea still lands. ★ FIX: call admit() at the point a cycle files a proposal row, and record the returned Decision in the cycle receipt so the suppression is auditable rather than invisible. ⚠ Design note from the builder: Decision.__post_init__ REFUSES to construct a rejection lacking a matched id, fingerprint and reason, so silent dropping is structurally impossible — preserve that when wiring it.

PROPOSAL from seat s35-outofideas: wire out_of_ideas.route_reports() into health.py as a condition (c_routes_have_ideas) with an EXPLICIT CONDITION_ON_RED classification — an `unmeasurable` route must reach the board as needing attention, never as green. ⛔ NOT DONE IN THE BUILDING CYCLE ON PURPOSE: health.py regenerates health.json and a sibling seat was editing health.py in the same cycle, and the blocking-vs-advisory classification is a judgement the driver owns (research-loop §1: a BLOCKING red stops a cycle, an `advises`/`redirects` red must not). The module exposes a stable one-call API, so this is small.

⛔ THE LOOP'S CLONE IS SHALLOW, AND IT CENSORS EVERY GIT-DERIVED INSTRUMENT. Measured 2026-08-28 by seat s35-outofideas: both stuck_clock.py and the new out_of_ideas.py are horizon-limited by it, so a route older than the horizon reads `unmeasurable` rather than measured — an absent reading, not a reading of absence (CLAUDE.md §4). Previously recorded in the same shape by the AUT-PD-052..059 sweep ('the shallow clone censors both git-derived instruments'), which is the second sighting. ★ FIX: `git fetch --unshallow` in the loop's working environment, then re-run `stuck_clock --check` and `out_of_ideas --check` and record what changed. It is one $0 command and it clears every censored reading in both modules. ⚠ Left to the driver because unshallowing mutates shared repository state while sibling seats hold worktrees off it.

REGRADE, blocked behind the unshallow above and filed so it is not lost: re-measure out_of_ideas.py's EMPTY_ROUNDS_TO_HUMAN=4 against real history once the clone is deep. The settling observation is the DISTRIBUTION OF EMPTY-ROUND RUNS ON ROWS THAT EVENTUALLY DID PRODUCE A MEASUREMENT — if rows routinely produce a measurement on the 5th attempt, 4 escalates work that was about to succeed. Not computable today, and the constant's docstring says so rather than implying the number was measured here. Same treatment for proposal_dedup's NEAR_DUPLICATE_JACCARD=0.30 once the ledger passes ~400 rows: re-run calibration_probe() and re-pin if the in-bucket ceiling (0.111 today) approaches the threshold.

⛔ A FOREGROUND BASH CALL THAT HITS THE HARNESS TIMEOUT LEAVES A LIVE CHILD, AND THE EXISTING HOOK CANNOT SEE IT. Measured 2026-08-28 by seat s35-outofideas, on itself: a mutation harness was launched in the foreground, hit the 2-minute Bash timeout, and the wrapper's SIGTERM killed the SHELL while ORPHANING the Python child — which then raced a second copy of the same harness over one scratch directory. The seat caught it only by diffing its scratch copy against the worktree and noticing the module differed MID-RUN; the logs of the racing run would otherwise have read like a clean result, which is AUT-PD-055's fabricated-but-clean shape arriving by a different route. ⚠ `.claude/hooks/no-detached-background.py` does NOT cover this: it refuses a bare `&`, and this call had no `&` — it was an ordinary foreground command that the harness, not the author, terminated. So the orphan is created by the TIMEOUT, and every long foreground command is a candidate. ⭐ CLAUDE.md §1's rule already prevents it (a long command belongs in run_in_background, whose exit is the wake) — what is missing is anything that MEASURES the violation, which is the fifth rule in this repository to be correct and unmeasured. ★ CANDIDATE FIXES, to be chosen with evidence rather than taste: (a) a hook that refuses a foreground Bash call whose command matches the long-running shapes (a test harness, a suite, a preflight) rather than trying to predict duration; (b) `setsid`/process-group termination so the wrapper's signal reaches the whole group; (c) a seat-scoped lockfile in the scratch directory so a second harness refuses to start while a first holds it — which also closes the racing half rather than only the orphan half. ⚠ AND NOTE THE SEAT'S OWN CORRECT MOVE, worth keeping in whatever lands: it killed the orphans with the BRACKET form `pgrep -f '[s]35-...'`, which cannot match the shell issuing it — the self-match trap CLAUDE.md §6 records costing two orphan poll loops and one killed gate run.

⛔ OUTWARD-FACING ENV READ, TWO-VALUED: scripts/aixiv_review.py:64 reads BASE = os.environ.get('AIXIV_BASE', 'https://aixiv.science'). An exported-empty or wrong value decides WHERE A SUBMISSION-ADJACENT REQUEST GOES, and the two-valued read cannot tell 'unset, using the default' from 'set but empty' (CLAUDE.md §4's env-echoed-default failure, which has already carried a fabricated verdict all the way out of this repository once). ★ FIX: apply research/autonomy/envread.py's https_url and fail closed. ⚠ FILED RATHER THAN FIXED BY THE SEAT THAT FOUND IT, deliberately: it sits on the publication path, and CLAUDE.md §3 reserves outward-facing changes for a deliberate act rather than a seat's incidental cleanup. Small, but it wants the driver's eyes.

PROPOSAL from seat s34-healthaxes: give the cycle receipt an `escalation_raised: [<condition keys>]` field, so a future health condition can MEASURE whether the §3 escalation path was actually taken. ⛔ THE GAP IT CLOSES: health.py now computes and mails an `escalations` list, but no cycle has yet PRODUCED a §3 block from one — the consumer is a sentence in research-loop §1, and a rule whose only enforcement is prose is the shape this repository has lost five times (subagent_width, the fan-out receipt key, the seat-scratchpad convention, the reader/writer key mismatch, the session-shape rule that was UNREACHABLE on the interactive path). Same treatment `stalls_are_named` already gave stuck_clock: an absent field must read UNMEASURED, never green.

ONE FACT, TWO PLACES: research/manuscripts/program/emc-autonomy-architecture.md §5.2's condition table has no `axis` column and no restart-intensity paragraph, while health.py now carries CONDITION_AXIS and RESTART_INTENSITY as code. The doc is the architecture of record and it wins over the skills, so the two must not drift — add the column and a §5.2.x paragraph pointing AT the code rather than restating N. ⚠ Needs PREFLIGHT_TESTS=1 (manuscript-adjacent, GOVERNED path) and a declared amendment, which is why the seat left it.

⛔ SCORE RESIDUE: ~13 hand-filed rows carry values the additive-term defect accumulated before AUT-PROP-036's fix landed (a660303). AUT-PROP-026 is off by roughly −1160 (≈13 spurious −90 applications); AUT-PROP-033/034/035/036/037/038, AUT-PD-026/028/030/031, AUT-078 each carry ~+0.9 per re-score of inflation, AUT-PROP-006 ~+1.70. ⚠ THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: the inflation had already INVERTED THE QUEUE — the top 15 rows were hand-filed process rows, several already done, with the best derived route row 78 points below, which is CLAUDE.md §0's failure (documentation outranking live work) arriving through arithmetic rather than judgement. ★ FIX: the base is recoverable from git history (the first commit each row appeared in); repair each row and carry `_score_correction` naming the evidence, or ledger_io.write_ledger will refuse the write — which is the gate working, not an obstacle to route around. ⛔ Do NOT clear the residue by widening TOLERANCE or by adding a standing correction note: the note must differ from the one already on the row precisely so it cannot become a licence.

⛔ `priority-weights.json:terms.fruitless_attempts` (weight −8.0) IS APPLIED NOWHERE IN priority.py. Measured 2026-08-28 by seat s36-admissibility: it is echoed as a hard-coded 0 in all 77 derived score_inputs blocks, and 46 rows carry attempts > 0 that buy them nothing. ⭐ SAME CLASS AS `subagent_width`, which governed nothing for days while a JSON field and one test asserted its value — a dial that exists, is documented, and is read by no code. ★ FIX: either wire the term in (and add it to admissibility.derived_score IN THE SAME COMMIT, or every row goes refused_underivable on the next write) or delete it and say why. ⚠ Wiring it changes scores materially — 46 rows — so it is a decision, not a cleanup.

PROPOSAL from seat s36-admissibility: give cycle receipts ONE machine-readable field recording the ledger score the cycle acted on, so the admission predicate can adjudicate receipts instead of reporting 0/52 coverage. ⚠ THE PROSE ROUTE WAS MEASURED AND REFUSED, and that measurement is the argument: 27 receipts quote a score in text, a regex extractor produced 29 pairs and 17 apparent mismatches, and hand-inspection found 16 were extractor artifacts (matching a neighbouring ledger id's digits — AUT-PD-020 → '20') with the 17th explained by a fix landing between reading and writing. A false-positive rate that high builds a gate whose first maintenance act is to loosen it. One field per receipt closes it honestly.

⛔ THE DERIVED-ROW GENERATOR TURNS A ROUTE'S CONCLUSION INTO QUEUED WORK, so the queue offers rows whose own text says there is nothing to do. Measured 2026-08-28 by CYC-0053-3217966b immediately after the additive-score fix (a660303) corrected the ranking — THREE OF THE TOP FIVE ready rows are this shape, and the top row overall is: AUT-013 (172.0, `kind: experiment`, `state: queued`, `_derived: true`) reads "Treat as landscape context; the ex-vivo result is banked and NEEDS NO FURTHER LOOKUP"; AUT-074 (152.0) reads "Report it as a CLOSED LINE: elevated and pan-essential is not an opportunity"; AUT-025 (152.0) reads "KEEP REGISTERED for automatic re-grade when EMC expression data lands" — a row that is waiting on the outside world by construction. All three are derived from systems/graph, all three carry last_evidence_utc in early August, and all three have been offered as takeable work every cycle since. ⚠ THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE DEFECT JUST FIXED, and it survives it: the scores are now honest and the STATE is not, so a corrected ranking still points a cycle at non-work. It is also AUT-PD-051's family (a row that is effectively finished still being offered), reached through the generator rather than through a missed closure. ⛔ DO NOT FIX BY HAND-EDITING THE ROWS — they are regenerated from the graph, so a hand edit is erased on the next priority.py --write and the lesson with it. ★ THE FIX BELONGS IN THE GENERATOR OR THE GRAPH: a route whose next action is a conclusion ("needs no further lookup", "closed line") or a registration waiting on the world ("keep registered for automatic re-grade") must derive a row in a parked or blocked state naming what it waits on, never `queued`. ⚠ AND THE HARD PART IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, not the state change: keying on phrases would be a grep over prose that the next re-wording defeats. Prefer a field on the graph node that says whether its next action is an ACTION, a CONCLUSION, or a REGISTRATION — and then the generator reads a field instead of guessing at English. Check whether systems/graph already carries something equivalent before adding one.  ✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s75-derivedstate, merged at 1eefaf77d). ⛔⛔ THE CLASS IS 39 ROWS, NOT THE 3 THIS ROW WAS FILED ON — half the derived queue, 36 of them `queued`: 23 CONCLUSION and 16 REGISTRATION-waiting-on-the-world, against 38 genuine ACTION rows. The measurement changed the fix from a patch to a state mapping, which is why the row demanded the enumeration first. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATOR EXISTED ALREADY and no grep over English was needed: `state.status` on every route, a closed vocabulary in systems/CONVENTIONS.md §4.1 pinned by the schema, whose own definitions say there is no takeable step (`parked` = failed with today's tools, `closed` = conclusively unworkable, `delegated` = someone else's). The generator read NONE of it — only `next.blocked_on`, which 11 of 77 routes carry, so the other 66 were born queued BY CONSTRUCTION. Three rival discriminators were measured and refuted, including `next.cost == '$0'` which has no signal at all (all 32 are $0). Precision was chosen over recall because the errors are asymmetric: a miss keeps the status quo, a false park HIDES A LIVE ROUTE.
